claim: MALPs express Csf1 at a much higher level compared to other mesenchymal subpopulations in bone.
source: Compared to other mesenchymal subpopulations, MALPs expressed Csf1 at a much higher level and this expression was further increased during aging.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data showing Csf1 expression patterns across cell types (Figure 1B) and qRT-PCR validation showing 10.2-fold higher expression in Td+ cells (Figure 1D).

claim: Csf1 expression in MALPs increases during aging.
source: Compared to other mesenchymal subpopulations, MALPs expressed Csf1 at a much higher level and this expression was further increased during aging.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data showing age-dependent Csf1 expression (Figure 1B) and qRT-PCR showing 5.3-fold increase in bone marrow from 10-month-old vs 1-month-old mice (Figure 1E).

claim: Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice have increased femoral trabecular bone mass.
source: These mice had increased femoral trabecular bone mass, but their cortical bone appeared normal.
evidence: Supported by microCT analysis showing increased BV/TV and BMD in CKO mice (Figure 2E and F).

claim: Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice have normal cortical bone structure.
source: These mice had increased femoral trabecular bone mass, but their cortical bone appeared normal.
evidence: Supported by microCT analysis showing no changes in cortical bone parameters (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).

claim: Depletion of Csf1 in the entire mesenchymal lineage using Prrx1Cre leads to a more severe high bone mass phenotype than depletion in MALPs alone.
source: In comparison, depletion of Csf1 in the entire mesenchymal lineage using Prrx1Cre led to a more striking high bone mass phenotype, suggesting that additional mesenchymal subpopulations secrete Csf1.
evidence: Supported by microCT data showing more dramatic increases in trabecular bone parameters in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice compared to Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice (Figure 3).

claim: Additional mesenchymal subpopulations beyond MALPs secrete Csf1.
source: In comparison, depletion of Csf1 in the entire mesenchymal lineage using Prrx1Cre led to a more striking high bone mass phenotype, suggesting that additional mesenchymal subpopulations secrete Csf1.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of phenotypes between Csf1 CKOAdipoq and Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice.

claim: TRAP staining revealed diminished osteoclasts in the femoral secondary spongiosa region of Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: TRAP staining revealed diminished osteoclasts in the femoral secondary spongiosa region of Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice, but not at the chondral-osseous junction nor at the endosteal surface of cortical bone.
evidence: Supported by TRAP staining and quantification showing 58% reduction in osteoclasts at secondary spongiosa (Figure 4A and B).

claim: Osteoclasts at the chondral-osseous junction are not affected in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: TRAP staining revealed diminished osteoclasts in the femoral secondary spongiosa region of Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice, but not at the chondral-osseous junction nor at the endosteal surface of cortical bone.
evidence: Supported by TRAP staining showing no changes in osteoclasts at COJ (Figure 4A and B).

claim: Osteoclasts at the endosteal surface of cortical bone are not affected in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: TRAP staining revealed diminished osteoclasts in the femoral secondary spongiosa region of Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice, but not at the chondral-osseous junction nor at the endosteal surface of cortical bone.
evidence: Supported by TRAP staining showing no changes in osteoclasts at endosteal surface (Figure 4A and B).

claim: Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice are resistant to LPS-induced calvarial osteolysis.
source: Moreover, Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice were resistant to LPS-induced calvarial osteolysis.
evidence: Supported by microCT and histological analysis showing minimal bone destruction in CKO mice after LPS injection (Figure 5).

claim: Bone marrow cellularity is reduced in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: Bone marrow cellularity, hematopoietic progenitors, and macrophages were also reduced in these mice.
evidence: Supported by bone marrow cell counts showing 18% reduction at 3 months and 43% reduction at 6 months (Figure 6A).

claim: Hematopoietic progenitors are reduced in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: Bone marrow cellularity, hematopoietic progenitors, and macrophages were also reduced in these mice.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry showing reduced LK cells and trends of reduction in LSK, MPP, and SLAM LSK (Figure 6E).

claim: Macrophages are reduced in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: Bone marrow cellularity, hematopoietic progenitors, and macrophages were also reduced in these mice.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining and flow cytometry showing 36%, 65%, and 51% reduction in Cd11b+F4/80+ macrophages at 1, 3, and 6 months respectively (Figure 6C and D).

claim: MALPs synthesize Csf1 to control bone remodeling and hematopoiesis.
source: Taken together, our studies demonstrate that MALPs synthesize Csf1 to control bone remodeling and hematopoiesis.
evidence: Supported by the combined findings of reduced bone resorption and hematopoietic defects in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.

claim: Csf1 is an essential growth factor for osteoclast progenitors.
source: Colony-stimulating factor 1 (Csf1) is an essential growth factor for osteoclast progenitors and an important regulator for bone resorption.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about Csf1 function.

claim: Csf1 is an important regulator for bone resorption.
source: Colony-stimulating factor 1 (Csf1) is an essential growth factor for osteoclast progenitors and an important regulator for bone resorption.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about Csf1 function.

claim: MALPs are marrow adipogenic lineage precursors that express many adipocyte markers but contain no lipid droplets.
source: Specifically, we identified a novel mesenchymal subpopulation termed 'marrow adipogenic lineage precursors' (MALPs) that expresses many adipocyte markers but contains no lipid droplets (Zhong et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Zhong et al., 2021).

claim: MALPs are precursors for lipid-laden adipocytes (LiLAs).
source: As precursors for lipid-laden adipocytes (LiLAs), MALPs exist abundantly as pericytes and stromal cells, forming an extensive 3D network inside the marrow cavity.
evidence: Based on previous characterization of MALPs.

claim: MALPs exist abundantly as pericytes and stromal cells, forming an extensive 3D network inside the marrow cavity.
source: As precursors for lipid-laden adipocytes (LiLAs), MALPs exist abundantly as pericytes and stromal cells, forming an extensive 3D network inside the marrow cavity.
evidence: Based on previous characterization of MALPs.

claim: MALPs are the most interactive mesenchymal cells with monocyte-macrophage lineage cells.
source: Interestingly, computational analysis revealed MALPs to be the most interactive mesenchymal cells with monocyte-macrophage lineage cells due to their high and specific expression of several osteoclast regulatory factors, including RANKL and Csf1 (Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis cited from Yu et al., 2021.

claim: MALPs highly and specifically express several osteoclast regulatory factors, including RANKL and Csf1.
source: Interestingly, computational analysis revealed MALPs to be the most interactive mesenchymal cells with monocyte-macrophage lineage cells due to their high and specific expression of several osteoclast regulatory factors, including RANKL and Csf1 (Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis and scRNA-seq data.

claim: MALP-derived RANKL is critical for promoting bone resorption during physiological and pathological conditions.
source: Studies from our group and others have demonstrated that MALP-derived RANKL is critical for promoting bone resorption during physiological and pathological conditions (Yu et al., 2021; Hu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Yu et al., 2021 and Hu et al., 2021.

claim: Td+ cells from Adipoq:Td mice express 10.2-fold higher Csf1 than Td- cells.
source: While Td+ cells only make up ~0.5% of bone marrow cells (Zhong et al., 2020), qRT-PCR analysis revealed that their expression of Csf1 is 10.2-fold higher than Td- cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Td+ cells make up approximately 0.5% of bone marrow cells.
source: While Td+ cells only make up ~0.5% of bone marrow cells (Zhong et al., 2020), qRT-PCR analysis revealed that their expression of Csf1 is 10.2-fold higher than Td- cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhong et al., 2020.

claim: Bone marrow cells from 10-month-old mice express 5.3-fold more Csf1 than those from 1-month-old mice.
source: Furthermore, bone marrow cells from 10-month-old mice expressed 5.3-fold more Csf1 than those from 1-month-old mice (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Lipid-laden adipocytes (LiLAs) do not express Csf1 at a detectable level.
source: Surprisingly, LiLAs did not express Csf1 at a detectable level.
evidence: Supported by snRNA-seq analysis of white adipose tissue (Figure 1F and G).

claim: Adipose stem and progenitor cells (ASPCs) and mesothelial cells are the major Csf1-producing cells in white adipose tissue.
source: Instead, adipose stem and progenitor cells (ASPCs) and mesothelial cells were the major Csf1-producing cells, albeit their expression levels were much lower compared to MALPs in the bone marrow (Figure 1G).
evidence: Supported by snRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Csf1 expression in ASPCs and mesothelial cells is much lower compared to MALPs in the bone marrow.
source: Instead, adipose stem and progenitor cells (ASPCs) and mesothelial cells were the major Csf1-producing cells, albeit their expression levels were much lower compared to MALPs in the bone marrow (Figure 1G).
evidence: Supported by comparison of snRNA-seq data from adipose tissue and scRNA-seq data from bone marrow.

claim: AdipoqCre targets MALPs and LiLAs, but not osteoblasts and osteocytes, in young and adult mice.
source: Our previous studies demonstrate that adipocyte-specific AdipoqCre targets MALPs and LiLAs, but not osteoblasts and osteocytes, in young and adult mice (Zhong et al., 2020; Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies (Zhong et al., 2020; Yu et al., 2021).

claim: Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice are born at the expected frequency.
source: These mice were born at the expected frequency.
evidence: Observational data from breeding experiments.

claim: Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice grow normally with comparable body weight, femoral length, and tooth eruption as control siblings.
source: They grew normally with comparable body weight, femoral length, and tooth eruption as Csf1flox/flox and Csf1flox/+ siblings, which are considered controls in this study (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by measurements shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Peripheral white adipose tissue appears normal in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: Their peripheral white adipose tissue also appeared normal, with similar adipocyte size, number, and vasculature as control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Csf1 mRNA level in CKO bone marrow is reduced to 43% of control bone marrow.
source: The Csf1 mRNA level in CKO bone marrow was reduced to 43% of control bone marrow (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Csf1 expression in cortical bone is not changed in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: On the contrary, Csf1 expression in the cortical bone was not changed (Figure 2D), suggesting that osteocytes are not affected in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Osteocytes are not affected in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: On the contrary, Csf1 expression in the cortical bone was not changed (Figure 2D), suggesting that osteocytes are not affected in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of change in Csf1 expression in cortical bone.

claim: There is no compensatory increase of Il34 in Csf1 CKOAdipoq bone marrow.
source: However, ELISA analysis found no change in IL-34 amount in the CKO bone marrow (control 1.27±0.44 µg/ml vs CKO 1.08±0.55 µg/ml, n=5–6 mice), suggesting no compensatory increase of Il34 in CKO.
evidence: Supported by ELISA measurements.

claim: Il34 shares a redundant role with Csf1 by binding to the same receptor Csf1R.
source: Binding to the same receptor Csf1R, Il34 shares a redundant role with Csf1 (Lelios et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lelios et al., 2020.

claim: Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice show significantly elevated bone volume fraction (BV/TV) at 3 months (1.7-fold) and 6 months (3.5-fold) of age.
source: Compared to control siblings, CKO mice showed significantly elevated bone volume fraction (BV/TV, 1.7-fold) and bone mineral density (BMD, 1.4-fold) at 3 months of age and additional accrual (3.5- and 2.0-fold, respectively) at 6 months of age.
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice show significantly elevated bone mineral density (BMD) at 3 months (1.4-fold) and 6 months (2.0-fold) of age.
source: Compared to control siblings, CKO mice showed significantly elevated bone volume fraction (BV/TV, 1.7-fold) and bone mineral density (BMD, 1.4-fold) at 3 months of age and additional accrual (3.5- and 2.0-fold, respectively) at 6 months of age.
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice show increased trabecular number (Tb.N) by 14% at 3 months and 31% at 6 months of age.
source: These changes were accompanied by increased trabecular number (Tb.N, 14% and 31% at 3 and 6 months of age, respectively) and trabecular thickness (Tb.Th, 27% at 6 months of age), and decreased trabecular separation (Tb.Sp, 13% and 26% at 3 and 6 months of age, respectively).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice show increased trabecular thickness (Tb.Th) by 27% at 6 months of age.
source: These changes were accompanied by increased trabecular number (Tb.N, 14% and 31% at 3 and 6 months of age, respectively) and trabecular thickness (Tb.Th, 27% at 6 months of age), and decreased trabecular separation (Tb.Sp, 13% and 26% at 3 and 6 months of age, respectively).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice show decreased trabecular separation (Tb.Sp) by 13% at 3 months and 26% at 6 months of age.
source: These changes were accompanied by increased trabecular number (Tb.N, 14% and 31% at 3 and 6 months of age, respectively) and trabecular thickness (Tb.Th, 27% at 6 months of age), and decreased trabecular separation (Tb.Sp, 13% and 26% at 3 and 6 months of age, respectively).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The reduced structure model index (SMI) confirms improved trabecular bone microarchitecture in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: The reduced structure model index (SMI) confirmed the improved trabecular bone microarchitecture in CKO mice.
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Femoral cortical bone structure, tissue mineral density (TMD), and mechanical properties are not altered in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: Meanwhile, femoral cortical bone structure, tissue mineral density (TMD), and mechanical properties were not altered (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by microCT and mechanical testing data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: No structural changes are detected in vertebral trabecular bone of Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: To our surprise, while MALPs are present in vertebral bone marrow (Zhong et al., 2020), we did not detect any structural changes in vertebral trabecular bone (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by microCT analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: MALPs are present in vertebral bone marrow.
source: To our surprise, while MALPs are present in vertebral bone marrow (Zhong et al., 2020), we did not detect any structural changes in vertebral trabecular bone (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhong et al., 2020.

claim: Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice have normal tooth eruption.
source: Like Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice, these Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice had normal tooth eruption (data not shown).
evidence: Observational data from phenotypic analysis.

claim: Femoral length is reduced by 13% in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice at 2-3 months of age.
source: Their femoral length was reduced by 13% (Figure 3A), indicating a defect in growth plate development.
evidence: Supported by measurements shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice have a defect in growth plate development.
source: Their femoral length was reduced by 13% (Figure 3A), indicating a defect in growth plate development.
evidence: Inferred from the reduced femoral length.

claim: Trabecular BV/TV is increased by 10.3-fold in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice at 2-3 months of age.
source: Their trabecular BV/TV and BMD were remarkably increased by 10.3-fold and 5.7-fold, respectively, due to increased Tb.N (2.3-fold) and Tb.Th (2.7-fold), and decreased Tb.Sp (49%, Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Trabecular BMD is increased by 5.7-fold in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice at 2-3 months of age.
source: Their trabecular BV/TV and BMD were remarkably increased by 10.3-fold and 5.7-fold, respectively, due to increased Tb.N (2.3-fold) and Tb.Th (2.7-fold), and decreased Tb.Sp (49%, Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Trabecular number (Tb.N) is increased by 2.3-fold in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice.
source: Their trabecular BV/TV and BMD were remarkably increased by 10.3-fold and 5.7-fold, respectively, due to increased Tb.N (2.3-fold) and Tb.Th (2.7-fold), and decreased Tb.Sp (49%, Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Trabecular thickness (Tb.Th) is increased by 2.7-fold in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice.
source: Their trabecular BV/TV and BMD were remarkably increased by 10.3-fold and 5.7-fold, respectively, due to increased Tb.N (2.3-fold) and Tb.Th (2.7-fold), and decreased Tb.Sp (49%, Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Trabecular separation (Tb.Sp) is decreased by 49% in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice.
source: Their trabecular BV/TV and BMD were remarkably increased by 10.3-fold and 5.7-fold, respectively, due to increased Tb.N (2.3-fold) and Tb.Th (2.7-fold), and decreased Tb.Sp (49%, Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Cortical bone is enlarged in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice.
source: Furthermore, their cortical bone was also enlarged. We observed significantly increased periosteal perimeter (Ps.Pm), endosteal perimeter (Ec.Pm), and cortical bone area (Ct.Ar) in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice compared to control mice (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: Periosteal perimeter (Ps.Pm) is significantly increased in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice.
source: We observed significantly increased periosteal perimeter (Ps.Pm), endosteal perimeter (Ec.Pm), and cortical bone area (Ct.Ar) in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice compared to control mice (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Endosteal perimeter (Ec.Pm) is significantly increased in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice.
source: We observed significantly increased periosteal perimeter (Ps.Pm), endosteal perimeter (Ec.Pm), and cortical bone area (Ct.Ar) in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice compared to control mice (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Cortical bone area (Ct.Ar) is significantly increased in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice.
source: We observed significantly increased periosteal perimeter (Ps.Pm), endosteal perimeter (Ec.Pm), and cortical bone area (Ct.Ar) in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice compared to control mice (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: Supported by microCT measurements shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The endosteal surface in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice is not as smooth as that in control mice, due to extensive trabecular bone remnants at the midshaft area.
source: Interestingly, the endosteal surface in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice was not as smooth as that in control mice, due to extensive trabecular bone remnants at the midshaft area.
evidence: Observational data from microCT imaging.

claim: Prrx1Cre labels the entire mesenchymal lineage cells in bone, including chondrocytes, mesenchymal progenitors, osteoblasts, and osteocytes.
source: Since Prrx1Cre labels the entire mesenchymal lineage cells in bone, including chondrocytes, mesenchymal progenitors, osteoblasts, and osteocytes, these data suggest that mesenchymal cells other than MALPs also produce Csf1 to regulate bone structure.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about Prrx1Cre specificity.

claim: TRAP+ osteoclasts in the secondary spongiosa are reduced by 58% in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: TRAP+ osteoclasts in the secondary spongiosa (SS) were remarkably reduced by 58%.
evidence: Supported by TRAP staining quantification shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Bone marrow macrophages (BMMs) from control and Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice generate similar numbers of osteoclasts in vitro.
source: Cells from both control and CKO mice generated similar numbers of osteoclasts (Figure 4C and D), suggesting that the differentiation ability of osteoclast progenitors is maintained in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
evidence: Supported by in vitro osteoclastogenesis assay shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: The differentiation ability of osteoclast progenitors is maintained in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: Cells from both control and CKO mice generated similar numbers of osteoclasts (Figure 4C and D), suggesting that the differentiation ability of osteoclast progenitors is maintained in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
evidence: Inferred from the in vitro osteoclastogenesis assay results.

claim: No significant difference is detected in Osterix+ osteoblasts at the trabecular bone surface in control and Csf1 CKOAdipoq femurs.
source: No significant difference was detected in Osterix+ osteoblasts at the trabecular bone surface in control and CKO femurs (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining and quantification shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: Mineral apposition rate (MAR), mineralization surface (MS/BS), and bone formation rate (BFR/BS) are comparable in control and Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: Quantification revealed comparable mineral apposition rate (MAR), mineralization surface (MS/BS), and bone formation rate (BFR/BS, Figure 4H).
evidence: Supported by dynamic histomorphometry shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Bone resorption marker (CTX-1) is significantly reduced in Csf1 CKOAdipoq serum.
source: Furthermore, bone resorption marker (CTX-1) was significantly reduced in CKO serum, while bone formation marker (PINP) was not changed (Figure 4I).
evidence: Supported by ELISA analysis shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Bone formation marker (PINP) is not changed in Csf1 CKOAdipoq serum.
source: Furthermore, bone resorption marker (CTX-1) was significantly reduced in CKO serum, while bone formation marker (PINP) was not changed (Figure 4I).
evidence: Supported by ELISA analysis shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) injection above mouse calvaria induces osteolysis that mimics bacteria-induced bone loss.
source: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) injection above mouse calvaria induces osteolysis that mimics bacteria-induced bone loss.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about the LPS-induced osteolysis model.

claim: MALPs exist in calvarial bone marrow.
source: Since we previously identified the existence of MALPs in calvarial bone marrow (Yu et al., 2021), we applied this osteolysis model to Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
evidence: Supported by citation to Yu et al., 2021.

claim: One week after LPS injection, there is a drastic increase in bone destruction in control calvaria, but very minor destruction in Csf1 CKOAdipoq calvaria.
source: One week after LPS injection, we found a drastic increase in bone destruction in control calvaria, but very minor destruction in Csf1 CKOAdipoq calvaria (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: Supported by microCT analysis shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Calvarial bone marrow is surrounded by a thin layer of cortical bone.
source: H&E staining showed that calvarial bone marrow is surrounded by a thin layer of cortical bone (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 5C.

claim: After LPS injection, normal calvarial structure, including suture and cortical bone, are mostly eroded and filled with inflammatory cells in control mice, but unaltered in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: After the LPS injection, normal calvarial structure, including suture and cortical bone, were mostly eroded, and filled with inflammatory cells in control mice, but unaltered in CKO mice.
evidence: Supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 5C.

claim: LPS-induction of TRAP+ osteoclasts in calvaria is mostly attenuated in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: TRAP staining revealed that LPS-induction of TRAP+ osteoclasts in calvaria is mostly attenuated in CKO mice (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: Supported by TRAP staining and quantification shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: MALPs-derived Csf1 is important for osteoclastogenesis in diseased bones.
source: Taken together, our data showed that MALPs-derived Csf1 is important for osteoclastogenesis in diseased bones.
evidence: Inferred from the LPS-induced osteolysis experiments.

claim: Bone marrow cellularity starts to decline in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice at 3 months of age (18%) and further reduces at 6 months (43%).
source: Interestingly, bone marrow cellularity started to decline in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice at 3 months of age (18%) and further reduced at 6 months (43%, Figure 6A), suggesting that hematopoiesis is suppressed.
evidence: Supported by bone marrow cell counts shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Hematopoiesis is suppressed in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: Interestingly, bone marrow cellularity started to decline in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice at 3 months of age (18%) and further reduced at 6 months (43%, Figure 6A), suggesting that hematopoiesis is suppressed.
evidence: Inferred from the reduced bone marrow cellularity.

claim: MALPs directly contact F4/80+ macrophages.
source: Immunostaining revealed that MALPs directly contact F4/80+ macrophages (Figure 6B) and that there are fewer macrophages in the CKO bone marrow (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining shown in Figure 6B.

claim: There are fewer macrophages in Csf1 CKOAdipoq bone marrow.
source: Immunostaining revealed that MALPs directly contact F4/80+ macrophages (Figure 6B) and that there are fewer macrophages in the CKO bone marrow (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Cd11b+F4/80+ bone marrow macrophages are reduced by 36%, 65%, and 51% in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice at 1, 3, and 6 months of age, respectively.
source: Flow cytometric analysis confirmed that Cd11b+F4/80+ bone marrow macrophages were reduced by 36%, 65%, and 51%, in CKO mice compared to control at 1, 3, and 6 months of age, respectively (Figure 6D).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) are reduced in the bone marrow of Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: In addition to macrophages, we also found that hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) are reduced in the bone marrow of Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice (Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Lineage-cKit+ (LK) cells display a significant decrease in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: While only lineage-cKit+ (LK) cells displayed a significant decrease, more primitive progenitors, such as lineage-Sca1 +cKit + (LSK) cells, multipotent progenitors (MPP), and SLAM LSK, showed a trend of reduction.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: More primitive progenitors, such as lineage-Sca1+cKit+ (LSK) cells, multipotent progenitors (MPP), and SLAM LSK, show a trend of reduction in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: While only lineage-cKit+ (LK) cells displayed a significant decrease, more primitive progenitors, such as lineage-Sca1 +cKit + (LSK) cells, multipotent progenitors (MPP), and SLAM LSK, showed a trend of reduction.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Monocytes and erythroid progenitors are decreased in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: Moreover, monocytes and erythroid progenitors were also decreased but other myeloid and lymphoid cells, such as neutrophils, eosinophils, B cells, and T cells, remained the same (Figure 6F).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Neutrophils, eosinophils, B cells, and T cells remain the same in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: Moreover, monocytes and erythroid progenitors were also decreased but other myeloid and lymphoid cells, such as neutrophils, eosinophils, B cells, and T cells, remained the same (Figure 6F).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Changes in bone marrow hematopoietic cells do not result in significant alterations in peripheral blood compositions and spleen weight in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: However, these changes did not result in significant alterations in peripheral blood compositions and spleen weight (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by CBC analysis and spleen weight measurements shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mice with Csf1 global deficiency show a reduction of bone marrow vasculature in the primary spongiosa area.
source: A previous study reported a reduction of bone marrow vasculature in the primary spongiosa area in mice with Csf1 global deficiency (Harris et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Harris et al., 2012.

claim: No obvious changes in marrow vasculature are detected in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: However, we did not detect obvious changes in marrow vasculature in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice (Figure 6G and H), indicating that Csf1 from cells other than MALPs regulates angiogenesis.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining and quantification shown in Figure 6G and H.

claim: Csf1 from cells other than MALPs regulates angiogenesis.
source: However, we did not detect obvious changes in marrow vasculature in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice (Figure 6G and H), indicating that Csf1 from cells other than MALPs regulates angiogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of vascular changes in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.

claim: MALPs-derived Csf1 is required for regulating hematopoiesis, particularly macrophage production, in the bone marrow.
source: In summary, MALPs-derived Csf1 is required for regulating hematopoiesis, particularly macrophage production, in the bone marrow.
evidence: Inferred from the combined findings of reduced bone marrow cellularity, HSPCs, and macrophages in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.

claim: Bone is maintained by a fine balance between bone formation by osteoblasts and bone resorption by osteoclasts.
source: Bone is maintained by a fine balance between bone formation by osteoblasts and bone resorption by osteoclasts.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about bone homeostasis.

claim: Osteoblasts are derived from bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs).
source: These two types of functional cells originate from different stem cell lineages, with the former derived from bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and the latter from hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs).
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about cell lineages.

claim: Osteoclasts are derived from hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs).
source: These two types of functional cells originate from different stem cell lineages, with the former derived from bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and the latter from hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs).
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about cell lineages.

claim: Crosstalk between mesenchymal and hematopoietic subpopulations plays a critical role in bone homeostasis.
source: Crosstalk between mesenchymal and hematopoietic subpopulations plays a critical role in bone homeostasis, and disruption of it shifts the balance of bone remodeling, leading to bone disorders (Raggatt and Partridge, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Raggatt and Partridge, 2010.

claim: Disruption of crosstalk between mesenchymal and hematopoietic subpopulations shifts the balance of bone remodeling, leading to bone disorders.
source: Crosstalk between mesenchymal and hematopoietic subpopulations plays a critical role in bone homeostasis, and disruption of it shifts the balance of bone remodeling, leading to bone disorders (Raggatt and Partridge, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Raggatt and Partridge, 2010.

claim: Osteoclasts are differentiated from monocytes in the myeloid subpopulation of hematopoietic lineage cells.
source: As a specific type of macrophage, osteoclasts are differentiated from monocytes in the myeloid subpopulation of hematopoietic lineage cells (Boyle et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Boyle et al., 2003.

claim: Csf1 is essential for osteoclastogenesis due to its actions in promoting proliferation, survival, and differentiation of monocytes and macrophages.
source: Colony stimulating factor 1 (Csf1), also known as macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-Csf), is essential for osteoclastogenesis due to its actions in promoting proliferation, survival, and differentiation of monocytes and macrophages (Stanley and Chitu, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Stanley and Chitu, 2014.

claim: The expression of Csf1r is low in immature myeloid precursor cells and increases as the myeloid cells mature.
source: The expression of its receptor, Csf1r, is low in immature myeloid precursor cells and increases as the myeloid cells mature (Tagoh et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tagoh et al., 2002.

claim: Receptor activator of NF-κB ligand (RANKL) is an indispensable cytokine for promoting osteoclastogenesis.
source: Receptor activator of NF-κB ligand (RANKL) is another indispensable cytokine for promoting osteoclastogenesis (Kong et al., 1999; Suda et al., 1999; Kim et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kong et al., 1999; Suda et al., 1999; Kim et al., 2000.

claim: Csf1/Csf1r signaling induces the expression of the receptor activator of NF-κB (RANK), a receptor for RANKL, to further facilitate the formation of mature osteoclasts.
source: Csf1/Csf1r signaling induces the expression of the receptor activator of NF-κB (RANK), a receptor for RANKL, to further facilitate the formation of mature osteoclasts (Arai et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citation to Arai et al., 1999.

claim: Csf1 can be expressed into a secreted glycoprotein, a secreted proteoglycan, or a membrane-spanning cell surface glycoprotein through alternative splicing and proteolysis.
source: Through alternative splicing and proteolysis, Csf1 can be expressed into a secreted glycoprotein, a secreted proteoglycan, or a membrane-spanning cell surface glycoprotein (Stanley et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Stanley et al., 2009.

claim: A spontaneous inactivating mutation in the mouse Csf1 coding region causes a complete loss of Csf1 protein.
source: A spontaneous inactivating mutation in the mouse Csf1 coding region causes a complete loss of Csf1 protein (Yoshida et al., 1990).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yoshida et al., 1990.

claim: Homozygous Csf1op/op mice are osteopetrotic due to osteoclast deficiency, but this bone abnormality recovers over the first few months of life.
source: The resultant homozygous Csf1op/op mice are osteopetrotic due to osteoclast deficiency, but this bone abnormality recovers over the first few months of life (Begg et al., 1993).
evidence: Supported by citation to Begg et al., 1993.

claim: A spontaneous recessive mutation (toothless, tl) in the rat Csf1 gene leads to a more complete loss of osteoclasts, resulting in more severe osteopetrosis than Csf1op/op mice with no improvement when rats age.
source: Similarly, a spontaneous recessive mutation (toothless, tl) in the rat Csf1 gene leads to a more complete loss of osteoclasts, resulting in more severe osteopetrosis than Csf1op/op mice with no improvement when rats age (Van Wesenbeeck et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to Van Wesenbeeck et al., 2002.

claim: Knocking out Csf1r gene in mice generates similar or even more severe skeletal phenotypes than Csf1 deficient mice.
source: Knocking out Csf1r gene in mice generates similar or even more severe skeletal phenotypes than Csf1 deficient mice (Dai et al., 2002), further demonstrating the important role of Csf1/Csf1r signaling in controlling bone resorption.
evidence: Supported by citation to Dai et al., 2002.

claim: Csf1 is expressed in a wide range of cells, such as fibroblasts, endothelial cells, keratinocytes, astrocytes, myoblasts, breast and uterine epithelial cells.
source: Past studies have demonstrated the expression of Csf1 in a wide range of cells, such as fibroblasts, endothelial cells, keratinocytes, astrocytes, myoblasts, breast and uterine epithelial cells (Sehgal et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sehgal et al., 2021.

claim: Osteoblasts synthesize both soluble and membrane-bound forms of Csf1.
source: Primary cell culture experiments indicated that osteoblasts synthesize both soluble and membrane-bound forms of Csf1 (Felix et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citation to Felix et al., 1996.

claim: Targeting expression of soluble Csf1 by osteoblast-specific promoter (osteocalcin) rescues the osteopetrotic bone defect in Csf1op/op mice.
source: Interestingly, targeting expression of soluble Csf1 by osteoblast-specific promoter (osteocalcin) rescues the osteopetrotic bone defect in Csf1op/op mice (Abboud et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to Abboud et al., 2002.

claim: Csf1 is expressed in osteocytes.
source: Csf1 is also expressed in osteocytes (Werner et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Werner et al., 2020.

claim: Mice with osteocyte-specific Csf1 deficiency show increased trabecular bone mass in tibiae and vertebrates.
source: Mice with osteocyte-specific Csf1 deficiency were generated using Dmp1Cre. These mice showed increased trabecular bone mass in tibiae and vertebrates (Werner et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Werner et al., 2020.

claim: The prevalent view is that bone forming cells, including osteoblasts and osteocytes, are the major producers of Csf1 to control osteoclast formation.
source: Therefore, the prevalent view is that bone forming cells, including osteoblasts and osteocytes, are the major producers of Csf1 to control osteoclast formation.
evidence: Based on synthesis of previous literature.

claim: Osteoclast formation is controlled by various mesenchymal subpopulations in a site-dependent fashion.
source: In our previous study of mice with RANKL deficiency in MALPs (Tnfsf11 CKOAdipoq mice), we proposed that osteoclast formation is controlled by various mesenchymal subpopulations in a site-dependent fashion.
evidence: Based on previous findings from the authors' work.

claim: Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice, similar to Tnfsf11 CKOAdipoq mice, exhibit trabecular bone phenotype but have normal long bone growth and cortical bone structure.
source: We found that Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice, similar to Tnfsf11 CKOAdipoq mice, exhibit trabecular bone phenotype but have normal long bone growth and cortical bone structure.
evidence: Supported by comparison of phenotypes between the two mouse models.

claim: Global Csf1 deficiency in rodents is accompanied by progressive chondrodysplasia of the growth plate and altered endochondral ossification.
source: These mice have shortened long bones, in line with previous reports that global Csf1 deficiency in rodents is accompanied by progressive chondrodysplasia of the growth plate and altered endochondral ossification (Harris et al., 2012; Devraj et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Harris et al., 2012 and Devraj et al., 2004.

claim: Chondrocyte-derived Csf1 regulates cartilage-to-bone remodeling during endochondral ossification.
source: These data imply chondrocyte-derived Csf1 regulates cartilage-to-bone remodeling during endochondral ossification.
evidence: Inferred from the phenotype of Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice.

claim: Osteocytes play a role in regulating cortical bone structure.
source: Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice also have thickened cortical bones, suggesting a role of osteocytes in regulating cortical bone structure.
evidence: Inferred from the cortical bone phenotype in Csf1 CKOPrrx1 mice.

claim: LCP-derived Csf1 might be sufficient for promoting osteoclastogenesis in vertebrae.
source: Since Csf1 is also expressed at a considerable level in LCPs, we believe that LCP-derived Csf1, which should not be affected in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice, might be sufficient for promoting osteoclastogenesis in vertebrae.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on expression patterns and phenotypic observations.

claim: Tnfsf11 CKOAdipoq mice show a strong high trabecular bone mass phenotype in the vertebrae.
source: On the contrary, while Rankl shares a similar expression pattern as Csf1 in the scRNA-seq data, Tnfsf11 CKOAdipoq mice show a strong high trabecular bone mass phenotype in the vertebrae (Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yu et al., 2021.

claim: Depletion of RANKL or Csf1 in MALPs results in a similar or even more severe osteopetrotic phenotype than depletion of those factors in osteoblasts/osteocytes.
source: First, depletion of RANKL or Csf1 in MALPs results in a similar or even more severe osteopetrotic phenotype than depletion of those factors in osteoblasts/osteocytes.
evidence: Based on comparison of phenotypes from different mouse models.

claim: Femoral trabecular bone mass increased in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice by approximately 73% at 3 months of age.
source: In this study, we found that femoral trabecular bone mass increased in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice by ~73% at 3 months of age, comparable to the trabecular bone mass increase in Csf1 CKODmp1 mice at 4 months of age (Werner et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by microCT data and comparison with cited study.

claim: Tnfsf11 CKOAdipoq mice develop osteopetrosis at 1 month of age while Tnfsf11 CKODmp1 mice at the same age have normal bone mass.
source: In our previous study, we found that Tnfsf11 CKOAdipoq mice develop osteopetrosis at 1 month of age while Tnfsf11 CKODmp1 mice at the same age have normal bone mass (Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yu et al., 2021.

claim: MALPs suppress bone formation.
source: Second, MALPs also suppress bone formation.
evidence: Based on previous findings from cell ablation studies.

claim: Depletion of MALPs results in de novo bone formation in diaphyseal bone marrow, which cannot be rescued by transplant of WT white adipose tissue.
source: Using a cell ablation model, we found that depletion of MALPs results in de novo bone formation in diaphyseal bone marrow, which cannot be rescued by transplant of WT white adipose tissue (Zhong et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhong et al., 2020.

claim: MALPs highly express two potent BMP signaling inhibitors, chordin-like1 (Chrdl1) and gremlin1 (Grem1), to suppress osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow MSCs.
source: Studies by Zuo et al. validated this phenotype and further identified that MALPs highly express two potent BMP signaling inhibitors, chordin-like1 (Chrdl1) and gremlin1 (Grem1), to suppress osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow MSCs (Zou et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zou et al., 2020.

claim: MALPs limit the overall trabecular bone mass to provide enough marrow space for blood production.
source: By acting on both bone resorption and formation, we believe that MALPs limit the overall trabecular bone mass to provide enough marrow space for blood production.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on the combined effects of MALPs on bone and hematopoiesis.

claim: MALPs highly express hematopoietic factors.
source: This is also consistent with our recent findings that MALPs highly express hematopoietic factors and that MALPs mediate bone marrow blood cell recovery after radiation damage (Zhong et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhong et al., 2022.

claim: MALPs mediate bone marrow blood cell recovery after radiation damage.
source: This is also consistent with our recent findings that MALPs highly express hematopoietic factors and that MALPs mediate bone marrow blood cell recovery after radiation damage (Zhong et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhong et al., 2022.

claim: RANKL is highly specific for mature osteoclast formation.
source: Unlike RANKL, which is highly specific for mature osteoclast formation, Csf1 has much broader actions in tissue development, homeostasis, and repair (Sehgal et al., 2021).
evidence: Based on established knowledge and citation to Sehgal et al., 2021.

claim: Csf1 has much broader actions in tissue development, homeostasis, and repair compared to RANKL.
source: Unlike RANKL, which is highly specific for mature osteoclast formation, Csf1 has much broader actions in tissue development, homeostasis, and repair (Sehgal et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sehgal et al., 2021.

claim: No obvious changes in bone marrow cellularity were noticed in Tnfsf11 CKOAdipoq mice.
source: Our previous study with Tnfsf11 CKOAdipoq mice mainly detected bone phenotypes due to suppressed osteoclast formation. We did not notice obvious changes in bone marrow cellularity in those mice.
evidence: Based on previous observations from the authors' work.

claim: Csf1 drives myelopoiesis from HSCs.
source: In line with the well-known fact that Csf1 drives myelopoiesis from HSCs (Mossadegh-Keller et al., 2013), these results further indicate that MALP-derived Csf1 plays an important role in hematopoiesis, particularly the production of marrow-resident macrophages.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mossadegh-Keller et al., 2013.

claim: MALP-derived Csf1 plays an important role in hematopoiesis, particularly the production of marrow-resident macrophages.
source: In line with the well-known fact that Csf1 drives myelopoiesis from HSCs (Mossadegh-Keller et al., 2013), these results further indicate that MALP-derived Csf1 plays an important role in hematopoiesis, particularly the production of marrow-resident macrophages.
evidence: Inferred from the hematopoietic phenotypes observed in Csf1 CKOAdipoq mice.

claim: A recent study using LeprCre to knockout Csf1 did not find any changes in mouse bone marrow cellularity, marrow blood cells (including HSCs and macrophages), and peripheral blood composition.
source: In contrast, a recent study using LeprCre to knockout Csf1 did not find any changes in mouse bone marrow cellularity, marrow blood cells (including HSCs and macrophages), and peripheral blood composition (Zhang et al., 2021b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2021b.

claim: MALPs express Lepr.
source: Since MALPs also express Lepr (Zhong et al., 2021), we acknowledge the inconsistency between those data and ours.
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhong et al., 2021.

claim: The secreted Csf1 isoforms are derived by differential proteolysis from the full-length precursor.
source: The Csf-1 isoforms are synthesized from a full-length and a truncated precursor (Pixley and Stanley, 2004). The secreted isoforms are derived by differential proteolysis from the full-length and the cell-surface isoform is derived from the truncated precursor encoded by an alternatively spliced mRNA in which the regions encoding the proteolytic cleavage sites are spliced out.
evidence: Supported by citation to Pixley and Stanley, 2004.

claim: The cell-surface Csf1 isoform is derived from the truncated precursor encoded by an alternatively spliced mRNA in which the regions encoding the proteolytic cleavage sites are spliced out.
source: The Csf-1 isoforms are synthesized from a full-length and a truncated precursor (Pixley and Stanley, 2004). The secreted isoforms are derived by differential proteolysis from the full-length and the cell-surface isoform is derived from the truncated precursor encoded by an alternatively spliced mRNA in which the regions encoding the proteolytic cleavage sites are spliced out.
evidence: Supported by citation to Pixley and Stanley, 2004.

claim: The N-terminal 150 amino acids of both Csf1 precursors are identical and sufficient for in vitro biological activity.
source: The N-terminal 150 amino acids of both precursors are identical and sufficient for in vitro biological activity.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about Csf1 structure.

claim: Immunostaining shows Csf1 staining in MALPs, suggesting that MALPs express the membrane form of Csf1.
source: In the companied article published together with this one, immunostaining shows Csf1 staining in MALPs, suggesting that MALPs do express the membrane form of Csf1.
evidence: Supported by reference to a companion article (Inoue et al., 2023).

claim: Bone marrow macrophages in op/op mice are partially restored by secreted Csf1 injections.
source: A previous study found that the scant bone marrow macrophages in op/op mice are partially restored by secreted Csf1 injections (Cecchini et al., 1994), indicating that bone marrow macrophages could be regulated by both secreted and membrane-bound Csf1, possibly originated from MALPs.
evidence: Supported by citation to Cecchini et al., 1994.

claim: Bone marrow macrophages could be regulated by both secreted and membrane-bound Csf1, possibly originated from MALPs.
source: A previous study found that the scant bone marrow macrophages in op/op mice are partially restored by secreted Csf1 injections (Cecchini et al., 1994), indicating that bone marrow macrophages could be regulated by both secreted and membrane-bound Csf1, possibly originated from MALPs.
evidence: Inferred from the rescue experiment with secreted Csf1 and the findings about MALPs.

claim: Adipogenic progenitors in the bone marrow are an important mesenchymal subpopulation that controls osteoclastogenesis.
source: Together with our previous analysis of Tnfsf11 CKOAdipoq mice, our research demonstrates adipogenic progenitors in the bone marrow are an important mesenchymal subpopulation that controls osteoclastogenesis.
evidence: Based on the combined findings from this study and previous work.

claim: MALPs might have broad roles in inflammation and tissue regeneration.
source: The general functions of Csf1 on monocyte lineage cells implicate that MALPs might have broad roles in inflammation and tissue regeneration.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on Csf1 functions.

claim: Csf1r is mainly expressed in monocytic subpopulations, such as monocytes, macrophages, and osteoclasts, in an age-independent manner.
source: Concomitantly, Csf1r was mainly expressed in monocytic subpopulations, such as monocytes, macrophages, and osteoclasts, in an age-independent manner (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: HSCs express Csf1r at a low level.
source: In line with previous reports (Grabert et al., 2020; Mossadegh-Keller et al., 2013), HSCs also expressed Csf1r at a low level.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data and citations to Grabert et al., 2020 and Mossadegh-Keller et al., 2013.

claim: Aging increases Csf1 expression in various cell types including mesenchymal cells (EMPs, LMPs, and osteoblasts), hematopoietic cells (macrophages, granulocyte progenitors, and red blood cells), endothelial cells, and mural cells.
source: Aging not only increased Csf1 expression in these cells, but also initiated its expression in some other subpopulations, such as mesenchymal cells (EMPs, late mesenchymal progenitors [LMPs], and osteoblasts), hematopoietic cells (macrophages, granulocyte progenitors, and red blood cells), endothelial cells, and mural cells.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: MALPs are markedly expanded in aged mice while EMPs and LMPs shrink in numbers.
source: In aged mice, MALPs were markedly expanded while EMPs and LMPs shrunk in numbers (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The scRNA-seq data predict an increased amount of Csf1 in mouse bone marrow during aging.
source: Thus, our scRNA-seq data predict an increased amount of Csf1 in mouse bone marrow during aging.
evidence: Inferred from the combined observations of increased Csf1 expression per cell and expansion of MALP population.

claim: In the bone marrow, Csf1 is expressed in MALPs but not in LiLAs.
source: Furthermore, a companied article published together with this one used qRT-PCR and immunostaining approaches to clearly show that in the bone marrow, Csf1 is expressed in MALPs but not in LiLAs (Inoue et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by reference to companion article (Inoue et al., 2023).

claim: Strong Csf1 expression is detected in Adipoq+ cells from control human bone marrow.
source: In addition, we also detected strong Csf1 expression in Adipoq+ cells from the control bone marrow (i.e. non-pathologic) acquired from a recent scRNA-seq study examining human multiple myeloma microenvironment (de Jong et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by analysis of human scRNA-seq data from de Jong et al., 2021.

claim: MALPs are the major Csf1-producing cells in bone tissue.
source: Taken together, our scRNA-seq data indicate that MALPs are the major Csf1-producing cells in bone tissue.
evidence: Inferred from the combined scRNA-seq analyses across species and tissues.
